findings.description: Epistemic flags formatted as inline italic paragraph rather than the standard block format used across all other scanned posts. Other posts use '**EPISTEMIC FLAGS**' with a horizontal rule and dashed list underneath. This post uses '*Epistemic note:*' as running prose. Breaks the structural convention readers rely on for locating epistemic qualifications.
findings.suggestion: Reformat to match the convention used in all other posts: a horizontal rule, then '**EPISTEMIC FLAGS**' heading, then a dashed list of individual flags. The content already covers the right topics — only the presentation format needs alignment.
findings.context: *Epistemic note: Fiscal estimates in this post carry high uncertainty ranges. No authoritative CBO score for ICESCR implementation costs exists...*

findings.description: Two posts cover substantially overlapping content without cross-referencing each other: '2026-03-13-pattern-generators.md' (developer/researcher focus) and '2026-03-15-pattern-generators-for-ai-minds.md' (narrative/accessible focus). Both address the 17 CPG principles, five-stage crystallization pipeline, and adaptive forgetting. A reader encountering both posts would find redundant exposition with no navigational guidance explaining the relationship.
findings.suggestion: Add a cross-reference note to each post. The 03-13 post could note: 'For an accessible narrative version of this analysis, see [Pattern Generators for AI Minds].' The 03-15 post could note: 'For the full technical treatment including trigger tiering and three-discipline evaluation, see [Pattern Generators].' This turns overlap into a deliberate lens-differentiated pair.
findings.context: Both posts: 17 CPG principles, five-stage crystallization pipeline, adaptive forgetting, Cattell Gc/Gf interface, dependency clusters

findings.description: The claim that 'Google processes billions of searches per day' cites internetlivestats.com — a third-party aggregation site without disclosed primary methodology. Fair witness standard calls for primary sources when available. Google publishes search volume data in SEC filings and official blog posts. The adjacent Meta citation (investor.fb.com) meets the primary-source standard; the Google citation does not.
findings.suggestion: Replace with a primary or authoritative source: Google's SEC filings, Google Trends documentation, or a peer-reviewed publication citing Google's own disclosures. Alternatively, hedge the attribution: 'Google reportedly processes billions of searches per day (various estimates).'

findings.description: The claim 'many organizations lack adequate auditability for AI agent decisions' attributes a specific finding about AI agent decisions to a McKinsey survey ('The State of AI in 2025') that primarily covers broader AI adoption patterns. The specificity 'AI agent decisions' may exceed what the cited source establishes — McKinsey surveys typically address AI deployment and governance at the organizational level, not agent-specific decision auditability.
findings.suggestion: Verify the McKinsey report addresses AI agent decision auditability specifically. If it covers broader AI governance, adjust the claim: 'many organizations lack adequate auditability for AI decisions' (dropping 'agent') or cite the specific finding from the report.
findings.context: Research suggests that many organizations lack adequate auditability for AI agent decisions (McKinsey, 'The State of AI in 2025,' Global Survey, 2025).

findings.description: Published prose includes an inline verification request: 'Comoros (which signed in 2008 but whose ratification status warrants verification against the UN Treaty Collection).' While epistemically honest, published content that explicitly asks readers to verify its own claims undermines editorial authority. The hedging belongs in an epistemic flags block, not in the running text.
findings.suggestion: Either verify the Comoros status before publication and state the result, or move the uncertainty to the epistemic flags block. In the running text, use a simpler hedge: 'Comoros (signed 2008, ratification status pending verification)' or omit Comoros and keep the focus on the clearer examples (Cuba, Palau, Nauru).
findings.context: Comoros (which signed in 2008 but whose ratification status warrants verification against the UN Treaty Collection)

findings.description: Title claims 'Cut Our AI Agent Costs by 52%.' The body (line 192) clarifies the 52% figure represents messages handled deterministically without LLM invocation — not cost reduction per se. The relationship between message handling and cost depends on per-invocation pricing, token costs, and cycle frequency that go unstated. The body's epistemic flags section appropriately qualifies the figure as a single-run snapshot, but the title presents a cost-reduction claim the data does not directly support.
findings.suggestion: Adjust title to match what was measured: 'Moved 52% of AI Agent Work to Deterministic Code' or 'Handled 52% of Messages Without LLM Invocation.' The current framing conflates workload reduction with cost reduction.
findings.context: Title: 'Crystallized Intelligence as System Architecture: How a Psychology Concept Cut Our AI Agent Costs by 52%'
